programs.name: Michigan Choice Waiver Program
programs.tagline: Get comprehensive home care services if your loved one needs nursing home-level care but wants to stay home.
programs.intro:
If your loved one needs daily help with bathing, dressing, or medication management but wants to stay home instead of moving to a nursing home, Michigan Choice Waiver covers comprehensive home care services through Medicaid. Because this program covers everything from meal delivery to personal care under one coordinated plan, your loved one gets a dedicated care team instead of juggling multiple providers.

Your loved one must be 65+ (or 18-64 if disabled), have gross monthly income under $2,982 (2025), and countable assets under $9,950. They must also qualify for nursing facility level of care through a clinical assessment and need at least two waiver services including supports coordination. The program operates statewide through regional agencies, though waitlists vary by area.

Services are individualized based on your loved one's assessed needs and include adult day health, home delivered meals, personal emergency response systems, respite care, environmental modifications, and specialized medical equipment. You must contact your regional MI Choice Waiver Agency directly, there's no central application hotline.

summary: Must live in community (not nursing home)
structuredEligibility.functionalRequirement: Must meet Nursing Facility Level of Care (a clinical assessment of whether your loved one needs daily help with bathing, dressing, medication management, or has cognitive/behavioral needs requiring 24-hour supervision)
otherRequirements: Must need supports coordination plus at least one other waiver service
Must live in home or community setting, not nursing home
60-month look-back period for asset transfers applies

applicationGuide.summary: Call your regional MI Choice Waiver Agency for a phone screening, followed by an in-person assessment, processing time varies by agency.

steps.title: Find your regional agency
steps.description: Contact your local MI Choice Waiver Agency by county. For example: The Senior Alliance covers Wayne County at 734-722-2830, or find your regional agency on the state website directory.

steps.title: Complete phone screening
steps.description: The agency conducts a preliminary eligibility screening over the phone to determine if you should proceed to formal assessment.

steps.title: Schedule in-person assessment
steps.description: If preliminarily eligible, schedule the Michigan Medicaid Level of Care Determination (LOCD) assessment at your loved one's home.

steps.title: Gather required documents
steps.description: Collect income verification, asset statements, proof of Medicaid eligibility, and medical information before the assessment visit.

steps.title: Complete LOCD assessment
steps.description: Assessor evaluates your loved one's activities of daily living, cognitive abilities, and behavioral needs to determine nursing facility level of care.

steps.title: Wait for determination
steps.description: If approved and a slot is available, care coordination begins. If waitlisted, you'll be contacted when services become available.

applicationGuide.waitlist: Exists and varies by region, some agencies may have immediate openings while others have extended wait times
applicationGuide.tip: Contact multiple regional agencies if you're near county borders, some may have shorter waitlists than others.

faqs.question: Can my loved one keep their house if it's worth more than the asset limit?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as the home equity is under $730,000 (2025 limit) and your loved one intends to return home. The house doesn't count toward the $9,950 asset limit. If your loved one permanently moves out, the house may need to be sold.

faqs.question: What happens if my loved one's Social Security income is $2,990 per month?
faqs.answer: For 2026, the gross monthly income limit for the MI Choice Waiver is $2,982. If your loved one is over this limit, they do not automatically qualify for this specific waiver. However, Michigan is a 'medically needy' state. This means your loved one may be able to 'spend down' their excess income by applying qualifying medical expenses toward that limit to become eligible. Contact your local MI Choice Waiver agency or a benefits counselor to see if a spend-down strategy could work for your loved one's specific situation.

faqs.question: Can I apply for MI Choice Waiver if my loved one is already in a nursing home?
faqs.answer: Yes. While MI Choice Waiver is designed for those living in the community, you can apply while your loved one is in a nursing home if they want to transition back to the community. Contact your local MI Choice Waiver agency to discuss the 'nursing facility transition' process. They can help coordinate a move back to an appropriate community setting, such as a private home, apartment, or assisted living facility, provided the participant can be safely supported there.

faqs.question: How long is the waitlist really?
faqs.answer: Waitlist length varies significantly by regional agency and isn't publicly reported. Some agencies may have immediate openings while others have extended waits. When you call for screening, ask specifically about current wait times in your area.

faqs.question: Can I apply on behalf of my loved one who has dementia?
faqs.answer: Yes, family members can initiate the application process. However, your loved one will need to participate in the in-person assessment, and you may need legal authority (power of attorney or guardianship) to complete certain parts of the process.

faqs.question: What if we gave away $15,000 to grandchildren two years ago?
faqs.answer: This gift would likely trigger a penalty period under the 60-month look-back rule, potentially delaying eligibility. The penalty length depends on the amount given away divided by the average monthly cost of nursing home care in Michigan. Disclose all transfers during the application.

faqs.question: Can my loved one get both MI Choice Waiver and PACE services?
faqs.answer: No, you cannot be enrolled in both programs simultaneously. MI Choice Waiver and PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) are both comprehensive programs designed to help individuals avoid nursing home placement. Because they both provide coordinated, long-term care services, they are alternatives to one another. You should discuss both options with your local Area Agency on Aging or a benefits counselor to determine which program best aligns with your loved one's specific medical needs and preferred care providers.

faqs.question: What happens if my loved one's needs increase after enrollment?
faqs.answer: Care plans are regularly reassessed and can be adjusted as needs change. If your loved one requires more intensive care that exceeds waiver service limits, they may need to transition to nursing home care or consider other options like PACE.

programs.name: MI Coordinated Health (MICH)
programs.tagline: If your loved one has both Medicare and Medicaid, one coordinated plan covers all their medical care and home services.

localEntities.name: MI Coordinated Health participating health plans (service areas vary)

programs.intro:
If your loved one has both Medicare and Medicaid, MI Coordinated Health (MICH) combines all their benefits into one coordinated plan. Instead of managing separate Medicare and Medicaid providers, your loved one gets one care coordinator and one team handling everything from doctor visits to prescriptions to home care services.

MICH replaced the MI Health Link program on January 1, 2026. MICH plans operate under a Medicare Advantage framework, so coverage is tied to a specific plan's provider network and service area. Check the plan's provider directory before enrolling to confirm your loved one's doctors are included.

Enrollment is managed by the state. If your loved one is eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid, they will receive an enrollment packet from Michigan ENROLLS listing their plan options. Once enrolled, a Care Coordinator contacts them to assess their health and support needs, and handles the paperwork from there.

If your loved one is currently enrolled in MI Choice, PACE, or a similar program, they must leave that program before joining MICH. Speak with a benefits counselor or their current care coordinator first so their services continue without a gap in care.

Cannot be in hospice, PACE, or MI Choice

faqs.question: Can my loved one keep their current doctors under MI Coordinated Health?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether their doctors are in the network of the specific MICH plan you choose. Since MICH plans operate as Medicare Advantage plans, you should check the plan's provider directory before enrolling. If their current doctor isn't in the network, you may need to switch or see if the plan offers out-of-network options.

faqs.question: What happens if my loved one moves outside their plan's service area?
faqs.answer: MICH coverage is tied to specific service areas. If your loved one moves outside of these areas, their MICH enrollment will be terminated, and they will transition back to Original Medicare and traditional Medicaid. You should contact Michigan ENROLLS as soon as you know about a move to ensure coverage continues without a gap.

faqs.question: Can my loved one be in MI Coordinated Health and MI Choice at the same time?
faqs.answer: Generally, no. MICH is an integrated program that replaces separate Medicare and Medicaid managed care plans. If your loved one is enrolled in a specialized program like PACE or receives services through a MI Choice waiver, they typically must disenroll from those before joining MICH. Because these programs provide specific, coordinated care, consult with a benefits counselor before making any changes.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the different MICH plans available to my loved one?
faqs.answer: Compare the provider networks, care coordination approaches, and additional services offered by each plan. The enrollment packet from Michigan ENROLLS should include plan comparison information. You can also contact each plan directly to ask about their providers and services.

faqs.question: What if my loved one needs nursing home care after enrolling?
faqs.answer: MI Coordinated Health covers nursing home care, and the integrated approach means the same care coordinator who managed their home services will coordinate their nursing home placement and care. Your loved one will pay their usual patient pay amount to the nursing home.

faqs.question: Can I apply for my loved one who has dementia?
faqs.answer: Yes, family members can complete enrollment for parents who cannot manage their own healthcare decisions. You'll need to provide the required HIPAA consent forms and may need to establish legal authority depending on your loved one's capacity and the plan's requirements.

faqs.question: What happens to my loved one's Medicare Part D coverage?
faqs.answer: MI Coordinated Health includes Medicare prescription drug coverage. Your loved one cannot keep their separate Part D plan and will get prescription coverage through their MICH plan with no co-pays or deductibles on covered medications. This is typically better coverage than standalone Part D.

faqs.question: Is there a deadline to enroll or can my loved one join anytime?
faqs.answer: Enrollment happens through specific phases and opportunities. Eligible individuals receive enrollment letters with deadlines for making choices. Missing the deadline results in auto-assignment to a plan. Contact Michigan ENROLLS about current enrollment opportunities for your county.

programs.name: MI Options
programs.tagline: Free counseling to help your loved one explore home care options, Medicare plans, and long-term care services in Michigan.

localEntities.name: Statewide call center; local: The Senior Alliance (Wayne County), AgeWays, WellWise Services (regional examples)

programs.intro:
If your loved one needs help navigating Medicare options or exploring alternatives to nursing home care, MI Options provides free person-centered counseling sessions. Because these are certified counselors who specialize in aging services, your loved one gets personalized guidance on home and community-based services, caregiver respite, transportation options, and Medicare plan selection, all in one 90-minute session with follow-up support.

MI Options is open to all Michigan residents age 18 and older, including caregivers and family members. There are no income or asset limits. The program launched in 2025 and connects you to local Area Agencies on Aging and nonprofit partners statewide, but the counseling itself is always free.

applicationGuide.summary: Call the statewide number to schedule a counseling appointment, no forms or documents required upfront.

steps.title: Call the MI Options hotline
steps.description: Call 800-803-7174, Monday through Friday 8am-8pm. You can speak with an agent immediately, schedule an appointment, or get referred to a local counselor in your area.

steps.title: Schedule your counseling session
steps.description: The call center will connect you with a certified counselor through your local Area Agency on Aging or partnering nonprofit. Sessions are typically 90 minutes and can be done by phone or in person.

steps.title: Prepare for your session
steps.description: Think about your loved one's current situation, goals, and preferences for care. The counselor will create a personalized action plan and provide follow-up support.

applicationGuide.processingTime: Immediate phone access; counselor appointments scheduled via call center
applicationGuide.tip: Prepare a list of your loved one's current challenges and care preferences before the counseling session to make the most of the 90-minute appointment.

contacts.description: Schedule counseling appointments and get referrals to local providers

contacts.description: Local MI Options provider for select counties

faqs.question: Is MI Options the same as the MI Choice Waiver?
faqs.answer: No. MI Options provides free counseling and referrals to help you explore care options. MI Choice is a separate Medicaid waiver program that actually pays for home care services but has income limits and waitlists. MI Options counselors can help you understand if MI Choice might be right for your loved one.

faqs.question: Can I call on behalf of my loved one who has dementia?
faqs.answer: Yes. MI Options is specifically designed for family caregivers and includes you as part of the counseling process. The counselor will work with both you and your loved one (as appropriate) to develop a care plan that fits your family's situation.

faqs.question: What if my loved one already has Medicare, can they still use this service?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many MI Options users already have Medicare but need help choosing between different Medicare Advantage plans, understanding Medicare supplements, or exploring what Medicare doesn't cover for long-term care. The counselors specialize in Medicare navigation.

programs.name: Senior Project Fresh Program
programs.tagline: If your loved one is 60+ and on a limited income, they may qualify for $25 in fresh produce coupons from Michigan farmers markets.
programs.intro:
If your loved one is 60+ and lives in Michigan on a limited income, they may qualify for $25 in benefits to spend on fresh, locally grown produce at participating farmers markets and roadside stands.

To be eligible, they must be 60 or older (or 55+ and a member of a federally recognized tribe or urban tribal group in Michigan) and have a household income at or below 185% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, approximately $29,526 annually for a one-person household or $40,034 for a two-person household.

The program runs from May 1 through October 31, and benefits are loaded directly onto a digital card through the Healthy Together platform, so there are no paper coupons to manage. You can apply through the Healthy Together website or mobile app. If your loved one needs help with the application, they can contact their local Area Agency on Aging or Commission on Aging.

Age 55+ if member of Michigan federally recognized tribe

applicationGuide.tip: Each eligible household member can apply separately, so both spouses in a couple can each receive $25 in coupons.

faqs.question: Can I apply for my loved one if they can't do it themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes. If your loved one is unable to apply themselves, you can assist them as a 'proxy.' Because the program is now fully digital through the Healthy Together platform, you can help them navigate the online application or mobile app. You will need to use their account information to register, and you can then assist them with managing the benefits on their digital card. If you are shopping on their behalf at a farmers market, simply ensure you have their card and PIN.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss the October 31st deadline?
faqs.answer: Coupons expire on October 31st each year with no extensions. Any unused coupons cannot be carried over to the next year. You'll need to reapply when applications open again on May 1st.

faqs.question: Can my loved one get these coupons if they already receive SNAP benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, receiving SNAP or other food assistance programs does not disqualify your loved one from Senior Project Fresh. The programs can be used together to increase access to fresh produce.

programs.name: MiCAFE (Michigan's Coordinated Access to Food for the Elderly)
programs.tagline: Free help getting your loved one enrolled in SNAP benefits for monthly grocery assistance.

localEntities.name: Primary office: Elder Law of Michigan, Inc., Lansing, MI

programs.intro:
If your loved one struggles to afford groceries on a fixed income, they may qualify for SNAP benefits (Michigan Bridge Card) but not know how to apply. MiCAFE provides free, confidential help getting eligible seniors enrolled in food assistance programs they're missing.

Nearly 50% of seniors eligible for SNAP aren't enrolled, that's over 160,000 Michigan seniors still facing hunger despite available help. Because medical expenses reduce countable income for SNAP eligibility, many seniors on Medicare actually qualify but never apply.

MiCAFE trained specialists will assess your loved one's eligibility, help complete applications, and connect them to other programs like utility assistance and Medicare prescription drug benefits. All services are free, and they can even come to your loved one's home in some areas.

summary: Based on income minus medical expenses
Must be potentially eligible for SNAP
otherRequirements: Must be potentially eligible for SNAP benefits
All persons living together and purchasing/preparing food together count as one household

applicationGuide.tip: Emphasize any medical expenses your loved one pays out-of-pocket, these reduce countable income and may make them eligible even if their Social Security seems too high.

faqs.question: Can I call MiCAFE on behalf of my elderly loved one?
faqs.answer: Yes, family members can initiate contact with MiCAFE for their loved ones. However, your loved one will need to sign an Authorization and Consent to Release Information form before MiCAFE can discuss their specific situation or help with applications. This protects their privacy while allowing you to help coordinate their care.

faqs.question: What if my loved one's Social Security income seems too high for SNAP?
faqs.answer: Don't assume they won't qualify. SNAP eligibility is based on income minus medical expenses, so Medicare premiums, prescription costs, and other medical bills can significantly reduce countable income. MiCAFE specialists are trained to identify these deductions that many families miss.

faqs.question: Is there any cost for MiCAFE services?
faqs.answer: No, all MiCAFE services are completely free. This includes the initial consultation, application assistance, and ongoing support. The program exists specifically to help eligible seniors access benefits they're entitled to but might not know about or understand how to obtain.

faqs.question: Can MiCAFE help with programs other than SNAP?
faqs.answer: Yes, MiCAFE also assists with utility assistance programs, tax programs, Medicare Part D prescription drug benefits, and other community programs. They take a comprehensive approach to identifying all benefits your loved one may be eligible for, not just food assistance.

programs.name: Senior Companion Program
programs.tagline: Free companionship and daily living assistance for your loved one from trained volunteers age 55+

localEntities.name: Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan

programs.intro:
The Senior Companion Program connects older adults (age 55 and older) who wish to serve as volunteers with individuals who need extra support to maintain their independence. Senior Companions provide friendship, emotional support, and assistance with daily tasks to help your loved one remain at home.

Because the program is administered regionally, availability, specific service focus, and the exact populations served (which may include older adults, adults with disabilities, or those facing social isolation) can vary depending on the local agency in your county. This is a volunteer-led effort, distinct from professional, private companion care services that charge hourly fees.

While the program is free to those receiving services, it is best to contact your local Area Agency on Aging or the Michigan Association of Foster Grandparent and Senior Companion Programs to confirm whether a program is active in your specific county and to understand the referral process.

No income limits for families receiving care

Volunteers typically help with activities like grocery shopping, transportation to medical appointments, meal preparation, or simply providing socialization to combat loneliness.

Referral: while many participants are referred by family members, health organizations, or social service agencies, the program is a volunteer-led initiative, not a standard medical service

faqs.question: Can I request a specific type of companion for my loved one?
faqs.answer: Yes, providers match based on personality, interests, and care needs. Tell them if your loved one would prefer someone who shares hobbies, speaks their language, or has experience with their specific condition. Companions complete specialized training for conditions like dementia.

faqs.question: What if my loved one lives in assisted living or a nursing home?
faqs.answer: The Senior Companion Program is primarily focused on helping individuals remain independent in their own homes or community settings. While some local programs may have specific partnerships, it is not designed to operate in all nursing homes or assisted living facilities. You must contact the program provider serving your specific county to confirm whether they have the capacity to serve your loved one in their specific residence.

faqs.question: How do I know if my county has Senior Companion services?
faqs.answer: The Senior Companion Program is managed regionally. There is no single statewide office that maintains a live list of all active county programs. To see if service is available in your area, contact your local Area Agency on Aging (AAA). They are the central hub for senior services and can immediately confirm whether there is an active Senior Companion program in your county.

faqs.question: What exactly will the companion do during their visits?
faqs.answer: Companions provide friendship, light housekeeping, meal preparation, medication reminders, transportation to appointments, and help with errands. They cannot provide medical care or personal care like bathing, but they can assist with activities of daily living.

faqs.question: Can my loved one get a companion if they don't have a disability?
faqs.answer: Your loved one needs to meet the program's definition of special needs, which includes loneliness and social isolation. Many older adults qualify based on frail health or isolation, even without a formal disability diagnosis.

faqs.question: What happens if the companion match doesn't work out?
faqs.answer: Contact your provider immediately to request a new match. Providers understand that personality compatibility is crucial and will work to find a better fit. There's no penalty for requesting a change.

stateOverview.intro: Michigan offers 5 key programs that can help your aging loved one stay independent and reduce your family's caregiving costs. These range from comprehensive home care services (Michigan Choice Waiver) to free grocery assistance navigation (MiCAFE) to volunteer companionship. Most programs focus on seniors with limited income, but some resources like Senior Companion Program are available regardless of finances. Start by checking if your loved one qualifies for the Michigan Choice Waiver Program or MI Health Link, these provide the most comprehensive support and can save thousands in care costs. For immediate help, MiCAFE offers free assistance getting your loved one enrolled in SNAP benefits within days.

stateOverview.resourcesVsBenefits: Michigan offers both qualification-based benefits that require income/asset limits (like Michigan Choice Waiver and Senior Project Fresh for limited income seniors) and free resources available to anyone (like MiCAFE's enrollment assistance). The largest benefits require strict qualification criteria, while navigator services like MiCAFE can help any senior access federal programs regardless of their current benefit status.
